Estimate nuisance values for eSVD objects (i.e., over-dispersion)

Source: R/nuisance.R
estimate_nuisance.eSVD.Rd

Assumes a Gamma-Poisson model where the mean and variance are proportionally related: \(\lambda_{ji} \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\mathrm{mean} = \mu_{ji}, \mathrm{var} = \gamma_j \mu_{ji})\). The estimated nuisance_vec is the Gamma rate \(\beta_j = 1/\gamma_j\), the reciprocal of the over-dispersion \(\gamma_j\) in Lin, Qiu and Roeder (2024), so a larger value means less over-dispersion.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'eSVD'
estimate_nuisance(
  input_obj,
  bool_covariates_as_library = TRUE,
  bool_library_includes_interept = TRUE,
  bool_use_log = FALSE,
  cap_multiplier = 10,
  min_val = 1e-04,
  verbose = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

input_obj

eSVD object output from opt_esvd.eSVD. Specifically, the nuisance parameters will be estimated based on the fit in input_obj[[input_obj[["latest_Fit"]]]].

bool_covariates_as_library

Boolean to include the donor covariates (every covariate other than the case-control variable) in the covariate-adjusted library size, default is TRUE, as in compute_posterior.eSVD and compute_test_per_gene and as eSVD passes it. Pass the same value to all of them, or the rate and the posterior use different libraries.

bool_library_includes_interept

Boolean if the intercept term from the eSVD matrix factorization should be included in the calculation for the covariate-adjusted library size, default is TRUE.

bool_use_log

Boolean if the nuisance (i.e., over-dispersion) parameter should be estimated on the log scale, default is FALSE.

cap_multiplier

One positive number, default 10: no gene's rate may exceed this many times the median over cells of its library size. Inf means no cap.

min_val

Minimum value of the rate, as a multiple of the median over cells of the gene's library size (the units of cap_multiplier); must be below cap_multiplier. Default 1e-4.

verbose

Integer.

...

Additional parameters.

Value

eSVD object with the following named vectors, one entry per gene, added to the list in input_obj[[input_obj[["latest_Fit"]]]]: nuisance_vec (the rate after the floor and the cap, which is what later stages read; compute_posterior still floors it at a quantile and may rescale it), nuisance_mle_vec (the rate before the cap but after the floor, so for a failed gene it is the floor and not an estimate), nuisance_library_median_vec (the median over cells of the gene's library size, so the cap is cap_multiplier times this), nuisance_status (a factor with levels estimated, capped, boundary, failed; see above), gene_mean_count_vec (the gene's mean count over cells) and gene_sparsity_vec (the fraction of cells in which its count is zero). input_obj$param records nuisance_cap_multiplier, nuisance_num_capped (the number of genes whose rate the cap replaced, the boundary genes among them included), nuisance_num_boundary and nuisance_num_failed; calling the function again overwrites them. plot_nuisance draws these.

Details

The cap. Each gene's rate is the maximum-likelihood estimate, bounded above: \(\hat\beta_j = \min\{\hat\beta_j^{\mathrm{MLE}},\ c \cdot \mathrm{median}_i\, \ell_{ji}\}\), with \(c\) = cap_multiplier and \(\ell_{ji}\) the covariate-adjusted library size of gene \(j\) in cell \(i\). The rate has the units of the library size, which is why the bound is a multiple of it. The bound is a calibration device and not an estimate of the smallest over-dispersion in the data: a gene whose counts are no more variable around the fit than a Poisson has no finite maximum-likelihood rate, its posterior would collapse onto the fit, and its test statistic would be inflated. The bound limits how much more weight the posterior may give the fit for one gene than for the typical gene. cap_multiplier = Inf removes it and gives the rates of version 1.1.0, except that the floor min_val is now a multiple of the library size rather than an absolute number. cap_multiplier = 1 is close to, but not the same as, the bound of the version that accompanied Lin, Qiu and Roeder (2024), which was the largest library size of the gene and not a multiple of its median. recompute_pvalue changes the multiplier on a fitted object without estimating anything again.

The floor min_val is in the same units: no gene's rate is below min_val times the median of its library size. On the unit-free scale of plot_nuisance every rate therefore lies between min_val and cap_multiplier, and no gene is above its cap. min_val must be below cap_multiplier.

The status of each gene records what happened to it:

estimated

the gene keeps its maximum-likelihood rate.

capped

a finite maximum-likelihood rate exists and is above the bound.

boundary

no finite maximum-likelihood rate exists: the score statistic for over-dispersion, \(D_j = \sum_i [(A_{ji} - \ell_{ji}\mu_{ji})^2 - A_{ji}] / \mu_{ji}\), is not positive. Such a gene is set to the bound, whatever value the iterations of the estimate stopped at (which is what nuisance_mle_vec holds for it). With cap_multiplier = Inf it keeps that value.

failed

both estimation routes failed and the rate is the floor, min_val times the median of its library size.

Examples

set.seed(10)
sim <- generate_null(cell_per_person = 15, num_genes = 40,
                     num_individuals = 8)
esvd_obj <- initialize_esvd(dat = sim$obs_mat,
                            covariates = sim$covariates,
                            metadata_individual = sim$metadata_individual,
                            case_control_variable = "CC",
                            bool_intercept = TRUE,
                            k = 2,
                            lambda = 0.1)
esvd_obj <- reparameterization_esvd_covariates(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                                               fit_name = "fit_Init",
                                               omitted_variables = "Log_UMI")
esvd_obj <- opt_esvd(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                     max_iter = 5,
                     offset_variables = setdiff(colnames(esvd_obj$covariates), "CC"),
                     fit_name = "fit_First",
                     fit_previous = "fit_Init")
esvd_obj <- reparameterization_esvd_covariates(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                                               fit_name = "fit_First",
                                               omitted_variables = "Log_UMI")
esvd_obj <- estimate_nuisance(input_obj = esvd_obj)
summary(esvd_obj$fit_First$nuisance_vec)
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. 
#> 3.446e-04 3.449e-01 1.358e+00 2.718e+00 3.305e+00 1.329e+01 
table(esvd_obj$fit_First$nuisance_status)
#> 
#> estimated    capped  boundary    failed 
#>        37         1         2         0 
esvd_obj$param$nuisance_num_capped
#> [1] 3
